source_review.notes: Checked the Chandy-Lamport, lightweight asynchronous snapshots, and MillWheel papers plus current Apache Flink and Beam checkpoint, state, connector, monitoring, and runner documentation. All thirteen cited URLs returned HTTP 200. Aligned/unaligned and runtime-version behavior is attributed and separated from the general consistent-cut proof.

evidence: Reviewed sources S, operators O, channels E, barrier B_n, positions p_s,n, operator/timer state S_o,n/T_o,n, channel state Q_c,n, and metadata M_n.
Checked relevant input set I_o, arrived-barrier set A_o,n, first/last barrier times, pre/post channel sequences, and completion predicate use distinct meanings.
Checked checkpoint IDs, topology/attempt epochs, half-open source positions, bytes, KiB/MiB, seconds, and rates carry explicit units/conventions.
notation_and_syntax.notes: Logical snapshot, durable materialization, task acknowledgment, global completion, source commit, and external transaction are deliberately distinct.

evidence: Executed aligned-barrier-cut with Python 3.14.4 and reproduced snapshot L1,R1,R2; withheld L2; and final state L1,R1,R2,L2,R3.
Recomputed examples: alignment 17-2=15 seconds; 600*32=19,200 KiB=18.75 MiB; 40 GB/200 MB/s=200 seconds; 2 GB/200 MB/s=10 seconds using decimal units for the latter.
Recomputed Exercise 2: start delay 8 seconds, alignment 23 seconds, sync completion at 33, async-after-sync 37 seconds, and global duration 74 seconds.
Recomputed Exercise 3: 1,200*24=28,800 KiB plus 300*40=12,000 KiB gives 40,800 KiB=39.84375 MiB.
numerical_recomputation.notes: Arithmetic establishes illustrative base values only; storage overhead, compression, replication, skew, and production performance remain excluded.

evidence: Verified FIFO barriers partition each channel into a pre-barrier prefix and post-barrier suffix.
Checked alignment blocks marked suffixes while consuming every unmarked prefix, yielding all pre-cut and no post-cut transitions at the last barrier.
Verified unaligned equivalence additionally requires complete ordered nonduplicated channel state restored with the operator image.
Checked global completion requires every mandatory durable component plus one atomic completion record; local file/ack existence is insufficient.
symbolic_recomputation.notes: Proof premises include FIFO/control ordering, complete input membership, atomic record transitions, stable ownership, and tracked asynchronous continuations.

evidence: Reviewed failure before/after barrier receipt, logical snapshot, upload, acknowledgment, completion publication, sink prepare/commit, and source-position persistence.

Reviewed first/last barrier, simultaneous/interleaved/concurrent IDs, slow/finished/dynamic inputs, long records/callbacks, hidden futures, full buffers, timeout, cancellation, and stale acknowledgments.
Reviewed partial/corrupt/missing incremental objects, orphan uploads, local-worker loss, coordinator/storage failure, rescale, schema/topology changes, and restore mismatch.
Reviewed forged barriers/acks, stale owners, unauthorized trigger/cancel/restore/delete, cross-region state, exposed credentials, and corrupted-channel-state bypass.
boundary_and_adversarial_cases.notes: Cut consistency, persistence durability, global agreement, replay, external effects, liveness, and confidentiality are independent failure surfaces.

evidence: Traced checkpoint ID from coordinator through source positions/barriers, input alignment or channel capture, logical state/timer image, upload/ack, sink preparation, manifest completion, retention, and restore.
Checked every state/position/timer/channel segment and acknowledgment carries one checkpoint plus current attempt/topology identity.
Checked async persistence reads a stable version while live processing mutates newer state and partial/canceled images never become recovery truth.
Checked restore selects all components from one completed manifest and treats managed state separately from external-effect commit/idempotency.
invariant_checking.notes: Watermarks, offsets, barriers, checkpoints, savepoints, and sink transactions retain separate scopes and consequences.

evidence: Reviewed the ten-step audit from recovery contract/source cut through channel order, operator atomicity, multi-input cut, logical snapshot, completion, effects, lifecycle, and fault evidence.
Checked the aligned proof and counterexamples for snapshot-on-first-barrier, process-early-suffix, and block-all-inputs.
Checked unaligned proof moves consistency obligation into captured ordered channel state rather than eliminating buffering.
Checked global completion and external-effect arguments reject inference from local acknowledgment or managed-state exactly-once.
proof_review.notes: General proofs are scoped independently from current Flink aligned/unaligned implementations and Beam bundle contracts.

evidence: Audited uses of consistent, atomic, durable, complete, exactly-once, aligned, unaligned, asynchronous, replayable, transactional, and idempotent.
Confirmed exactly-once is scoped to restored managed state unless sources/sinks/effects satisfy added contracts.
Confirmed unaligned latency, incremental size, local recovery, savepoint, watermark, and concurrent-checkpoint claims retain version/assumption boundaries.
Confirmed the executable trace disclaims concurrency, async work, backpressure, channel state, durability, coordination, restore, and sinks.
proof_sketch_labeling.notes: No successful upload, barrier passage, or restore is mislabeled as global completion or semantic correctness by itself.

evidence: Reviewed metrics for start delay, alignment, sync/async phases, state/channel bytes, upload, acknowledgments, global duration/age, failures, cancellations, and cleanup.
Reviewed correlations with busy/backpressured/idle time, buffers, skew, record/callback duration, storage/GC/CPU/disk/network, sink transactions, and topology.
Confirmed no universal interval, timeout, concurrency, aligned/unaligned mode, buffer size, retention, compression, or storage strategy is prescribed.
Confirmed selection requires representative state/traffic/backpressure, storage bandwidth, restore/catch-up targets, connector/sink support, topology, security, and fault tests.
empirical_evidence_labeling.notes: The local simulator and arithmetic are not production evidence for checkpoint duration, recovery objectives, or end-to-end delivery.

conceptual_review.notes: Reviewed recovery cuts, source injection, channel ordering, one/multi-input handling, aligned proof, async work, at-least-once nonalignment, unaligned channel state, watermarks/timers, atomic completion, cancellation, concurrency, sinks, capacity, observability, security, and fault validation.

practitioner_review.notes: Reviewed connector ordering/replay, stable epochs, hidden async queues, state versioning, durable handles/manifests, timeout/concurrency, aligned-versus-unaligned diagnosis, incremental dependencies, sink protocols, catch-up headroom, telemetry, access control, corruption response, and restore drills. Internal practitioner-oriented review only.

pedagogical_review.notes: Verified progression from cut semantics through barriers, alignment, channel snapshots, completion, effects, and operations. Ten examples and five answered exercises cover prefix mismatch, two-input cuts, timing, bytes, upload, intervals, async work, partial completion, sink transactions, and an executable alignment trace.

limitations: Internal evidence record only; no external Chandy-Lamport/Flink/MillWheel/Beam researcher or maintainer, distributed-systems/database/storage/network engineer, SRE/performance engineer, connector/sink owner, security/privacy/compliance specialist, tenant/region authority, accessibility specialist, or certification review is claimed.
